correctness.rationale: For independent unit row constraints the full scalar Schur pivots equal the Cholesky/Gram–Schmidt residual norms. The symmetrically preconditioned arrow spectrum is exactly the signed quadratic map of singular values. The 3-by-3 normalized row Gram has determinant 1 and the three permutation classes have exact characteristic coefficients as given. Strict polynomial sign comparison above each preceding maximal root yields the strict ordering for all t in (0,1); an exact endpoint argument gives ratios 5/4 and sqrt(5)/2. Two-row trace/determinant invariance proves minimality. Exact rational coefficient checks and full matrix eigenvalue crosschecks were run, not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The derivation isolates and proves a new cross-order optimization problem: strict spectral-radius ordering of all six permutations for a continuous exact-Schur three-constraint saddle family; the least-correlated pair is the worst first pair. The existing general Schur and eigenvalue relations are acknowledged. Comparisons with the closest primary full texts, general published preconditioner literature, accessible prior claims, and published mathematical results did not identify a covering statement. Priority remains provisional because two older abstracts could not be expanded to full text.
residual_risks: Older broad saddle-point preconditioning articles (Golub–Greif–Varah and Notay) were available only in abstract/metadata form; a more specialized ordering theorem could remain unseen.
General Schur complement and singular-value spectral relations are established; originality is confined to the new all-order optimization and sharp comparison, not these known ingredients.
No global ordering rule or MINRES convergence rate is established outside the named continuous family.

value.rationale: Permutation choice is a natural design question in the forward full-Schur block diagonal saddle-point preconditioner, where subsequent pivot sizes change with ordering. This continuous 3-constraint classification is the smallest nontrivial ordering effect, invalidates the seemingly natural least-correlated-first heuristic, and quantifies its nonvanishing spectral penalty in a nearly dependent limit. The precise result informs preconditioner diagnostics but does not claim iteration-count or floating-point benefits.
